findings.title: Mileage reimbursement POST declares no security
findings.evidence: "security":[] while the operation creates financial reimbursements; every other operation requires oauth2 scopes, and the only documented error is 401 Unauthorized.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the empty security override so it inherits oauth2 and add the reimbursements:write scope.

findings.title: Vault card endpoint returns PAN and CVV with read-only scope
findings.evidence: Response is CardDetails containing pan and cvv, but no description warns about sensitivity, and the endpoint has no error responses for 401/403 or rate limiting.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the sensitivity of pan/cvv, require a dedicated scope, and document 401/403 responses.

findings.title: Terminate/suspend/unsuspend operations have no 404 responses
findings.evidence: Path parameter card_id is required, yet only 400 and 200/204 responses are listed; no 404 for an unknown card.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 404 responses using DeveloperApiErrorResponse for unknown card IDs and document 401/403.

findings.title: Get virtual card operation summary is wrong
findings.evidence: "summary":"Permanently delete this resource" on a GET operation that returns a VirtualCard.
findings.suggested_fix: Change summary to 'Fetch a virtual card'.

findings.title: Physical card GET returns 201 instead of 200
findings.evidence: responses contains "201":{"description":"Success"} for a read operation; no 200 is declared.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the success response to 200.

findings.title: Physical card create response is 200 while vault create is 201
findings.evidence: Creation returns "200" with PhysicalCard, whereas POST /developer/v1/cards/vault returns "201" and POST reimbursement receipt returns "201".
findings.suggested_fix: Use 201 for resource creation consistently and document it.

findings.title: Vault create response schema is PCILimit, not a card
findings.evidence: Summary says 'Create a spend limit and retrieve sensitive card details' while the 201 schema is PCILimit whose card field contains PCICardDetails; the request also uses different schema names.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify in the description that the response is a limit containing card details and rename the response to reflect that.

findings.title: Physical card POST error response schema is a bare string
findings.evidence: 400 response: "description":"Error","content":{"application/json":{"schema":{"type":"string"}}}, unlike other endpoints that use DeveloperApiErrorResponse.
findings.suggested_fix: Use DeveloperApiErrorResponse for the 400 response and include x-trace-id header.

findings.title: Missing error responses across most operations
findings.location: Multiple operations, e.g. GET /developer/v1/cards/virtual, GET /developer/v1/reimbursements, PATCH /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id}
findings.evidence: Only some operations declare 400/401/404 with DeveloperApiErrorResponse; list and PATCH operations declare only 200, although security scopes imply 401/403.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a consistent set of error responses (400, 401, 403, 404, 429) using DeveloperApiErrorResponse to every operation.

findings.title: Inconsistent error shape: 400 descriptions vs schemas
findings.location: Multiple 400 responses, e.g. 'raises CardInvalidInput' and 'raises TransactionInvalidInput'
findings.evidence: Descriptions reference internal exception class names such as CardInvalidInput rather than describing the condition.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace internal exception names with human-readable descriptions of when the error occurs.

findings.title: Inconsistent naming for user filter parameter
findings.evidence: Parameter 'userId' is camelCase while all sibling params use snake_case, e.g. user_id on physical cards and reimbursements.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to user_id, keeping userId as a deprecated alias if needed.

findings.title: Inconsistent camelCase query parameter
findings.evidence: Other sort flags are order_by_amount_desc and order_by_date_asc (snake_case), but orderByAmountAsc is camelCase.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to order_by_amount_asc.

findings.title: Duplicate tags for transactions
findings.evidence: Top-level tags include both "Transaction" and "transactions"; PATCH /developer/v1/transactions/{transaction_id} uses both tags.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the lowercase 'transactions' tag and use one tag consistently.

findings.title: Pagination inconsistent across list endpoints
findings.evidence: Physical cards and reimbursements responses have no page_size or start parameter in physical cards, and physical cards return only a next link with no start/page_size parameters, while virtual cards and reimbursements define start/page_size.
findings.suggested_fix: Give all list endpoints the same pagination parameters (start, page_size with min/max bounds) and response shape.

findings.title: Physical card list has no pagination parameters
findings.evidence: Description says 'Returns a paginated list' but parameters are only user_id, display_name, include_activated_only, include_terminated_only; response contains a page.next link.
findings.suggested_fix: Add start and page_size parameters with documented bounds and default.

findings.title: page_size bounds not enforced in schema
findings.evidence: Description says 'must be between 2 and 100' but schema is only {default:20,type:integer} with no minimum or maximum.
findings.suggested_fix: Add minimum: 2 and maximum: 100 to the schema.

findings.title: Pagination cursor 'start' is not defined as opaque
findings.location: start query parameter on list endpoints
findings.evidence: Description says 'The ID of the last entity of the previous page', yet the response page.next is a full URL, so clients must choose between building the URL and passing start.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe start as an opaque cursor from page.next and document that it should not be constructed manually.

findings.title: Next page link is a placeholder template
findings.evidence: Examples show "next":"https://api.ramp.com/developer/v1/<resources>?<new_params>".
findings.suggested_fix: Provide a concrete example URL and document that next is null on the last page.

findings.title: Transaction list has inconsistent sort parameters
findings.evidence: Description says 'setting multiple ordering parameters is unsupported' but no default ordering or conflict behavior is documented; order_by_date_asc/desc descriptions say 'in ISO8601 format' which is irrelevant to a boolean.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the default sort, what happens with multiple ordering flags, and remove the ISO8601 wording from boolean sort flags.

findings.title: Boolean default contradicts description for activated cards
findings.evidence: Description says 'Defaults to True if not specified' but the schema has no default field, so generated clients will not apply it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add default: true to the schema.

findings.title: Reimbursement list state filter description ambiguous
findings.evidence: Description is just 'Data.' for to_transaction_date and include_merchant_data/trip_id on transaction detail similarly say 'Data.'
findings.suggested_fix: Replace placeholder descriptions with real text explaining the filter semantics and inclusivity.

findings.title: Reimbursement list filters use inconsistent date semantics
findings.evidence: from_transaction_date says 'after this date' while from_date says 'created after this date' and transactions from_date says 'user_transaction_time after'; inclusivity is not stated.
findings.suggested_fix: Document whether bounds are inclusive and the exact timestamp field each filter uses.

findings.title: Deprecated and duplicate fields without consistent deprecation
findings.evidence: Transaction.amount is type number deprecated, but SingleTransaction.amount is type string, and limit_id/spend_limit_id are duplicates of fund_id.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the type of amount identical across schemas and document removal timeline for deprecated aliases.

findings.title: Monetary amounts mix representations
findings.evidence: Money appears as a number (amount), an integer minor unit (ApiSignedAmount.value), and a nested CurrencyAmount with amount and currency_code; ApiSignedAmount uses 'currency' while CurrencyAmount uses 'currency_code'.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize on one money object shape and field names across all resources.

findings.title: Request body amount limit lacks currency semantics
findings.evidence: CurrencyAmountRequestBody.currency_code has default 'USD' but is not required, and the amount description says 'in cents' even though currency may differ.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify that amount is in the minor units of currency_code and whether non-USD values are accepted.

findings.title: Transaction PATCH split uses unclear amount units
findings.evidence: Description says 'amounts (in minor units)' and example 5000 = $50.00, but the line item amount is unitless and there is no currency field, while the response uses signed amounts.
findings.suggested_fix: State the currency for split amounts and document how they relate to entity_amount.

findings.title: Transaction PATCH marked destructive and non-read-only with no idempotency
findings.evidence: Operation has "x-destructive":true and replaces splits, but no X-Idempotency-Key parameter is offered and the 200 response is the only response.
findings.suggested_fix: Document that the PATCH replaces splits and whether retries are safe, and add error responses for failed validation.

findings.title: Idempotency keys inconsistently supported
findings.location: POST /developer/v1/cards/vault header X-Idempotency-Key; POST /developer/v1/reimbursement/submit-receipt body idempotency_key; POST /developer/v1/cards/physical
findings.evidence: Vault create takes an optional X-Idempotency-Key header, receipt upload takes a required idempotency_key body field, and physical card create/mileage create take none, though all are creating resources.
findings.suggested_fix: Adopt one idempotency mechanism (header) across all POST endpoints and make it documented and consistently required or optional.

findings.title: Receipt upload path uses singular 'reimbursement' unlike other paths
findings.evidence: Other paths use /developer/v1/reimbursements (plural); this one is /developer/v1/reimbursement/submit-receipt.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to /developer/v1/reimbursements/receipts or similar plural form.

findings.title: Path naming for card resources is inconsistent
findings.evidence: Suspension is a noun-based sub-resource where POST suspends and DELETE unsuspends; the card vault uses 'vault' as a resource while reading sensitive details uses GET on the same path.
findings.suggested_fix: Use consistent action or sub-resource naming, e.g. POST /suspension and DELETE /suspension is acceptable but document it clearly.

findings.title: Card sensitivity and ID parameter on PATCH lacks documentation
findings.evidence: Update accepts display_name but description says 'If a card is associated with a single spend limit, its display name will use the spend limit's display name' without explaining what happens to the stored value.
findings.suggested_fix: Explain precedence between display_name and the spend limit display name.

findings.title: Physical card response has nullable required fields
findings.evidence: required includes fulfillment and fund_id-dependent fields, but fund_id and fulfillment are nullable; PhysicalCard.shipping fields are null in examples.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark nullability consistently and remove required fields that can be absent.

findings.title: Transaction response has merchant_name required but readOnly
findings.evidence: Required list includes readOnly fields such as sync_status and updated_at while the same fields are nullable or absent in examples.
findings.suggested_fix: Review required list against nullable and readOnly markers so clients know which fields are always present.
